pr_title: resolved: support RFC 9460 SVCB and HTTPS records
pr_body:
This adds support for the SVCB and HTTPS presentation format in resolvectl. Closes #30624.

~~Includes #30513 just to avoid conflicts rebasing things, so also marking WIP for now.~~ But, I think it is in working shape:

```
$ dig @_localdnsstub +noall +ans HTTPS cloudflare.com
cloudflare.com.		295	IN	HTTPS	1 . alpn="h3,h2" ipv4hint=104.16.132.229,104.16.133.229 ipv6hint=2606:4700::6810:84e5,2606:4700::6810:85e5
$ ./build/resolvectl --legend=no query -t HTTPS cloudflare.com
cloudflare.com IN HTTPS 1 . alpn=h3,h2 ipv4hint=104.16.132.229,104.16.133.229 ipv6hint=2606:4700::6810:84e5,2606:4700::6810:85e5 -- link: enp7s0
```

issue_context.title: Support `HTTPS` typed DNS query
issue_context.body:
### Component

resolvectl, systemd-resolved

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe

With a systemd-resolved server running at `127.0.0.56:53`, `resolvectl query -t HTTPS cp.cloudflare.com` fails with this error message

```
Failed to parse RR record type HTTPS: Invalid argument
```

Meanwhile using a different DNS client like `drill cp.cloudflare.com @127.0.0.56 HTTPS` would succeed. It seems systemd-resolved could forward this query to upstream servers.

### Describe the solution you'd like

With the Encrypted ClientHello becoming more popular, it'd be nice to have this new type of DNS records supported by systemd:

- `resolvectl query -t HTTPS <domain>` works like other supported types (A, AAAA ...)
- `resolvectl show-cache` shows this type of records for debugging cache

### Describe alternatives you've considered

I have no idea.

### The systemd version you checked that didn't have the feature you are asking for

255.1-1 from Arch Linux official repo

review_comments: please add unit test coverage for this in `src/test/test-escape.c`

there probably should be some validation here that the string doesn't carry control characters, or maybe even is valid UTF8? or alternatively, there should be escaping in place (via cescape()?) to deal with weird bytes

Sadly this field is explicitly _not_ valid UTF-8, there is actually a list of known values in iana: https://www.iana.org/assignments/tls-extensiontype-values/tls-extensiontype-values.xhtml#alpn-protocol-ids, several reserved values have non utf-8 byte sequences. Seems like the useful values are human-readable strings though — so yeah I think c-style escape here will do.

I'll fix this.

we usually start out validity check functions with a check if the specified parameter is NULL or not.

i.e. add `if (!i) return false` here as first check?

Well I actually just return `value` from here after the break, so it seems like its actually the other oom checks on strv_join in the other case:'s that are superfluous. I don't mind just adding one here for consistency and clarity though I guess.

## Potentially uninitialized local variable using the cleanup attribute

The variable [i](1) may not be initialized here, but has a cleanup handler.

[Show more details](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/security/code-scanning/2334)
